definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese festival day marking seasonal transitions, originally derived from Chinese calendar customs. There are five major seasonal festivals throughout the year.

examples.japanese: ⟦{五月|ごがつ}→五月：00625_gogatsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{節句|せっく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{祝|いわ}う→祝う：01881_iwau⟧。
examples.english: To celebrate the May seasonal festival.

examples.japanese: {桃|もも}の{節句|せっく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{雛人形|ひなにんぎょう}→雛人形：14830_hinaningyou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飾|かざ}る→飾る：01185_kazaru⟧。
examples.english: We display hina dolls for the Peach Festival.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{五|いつ}つ→五つ：02892_itsutsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{節句|せっく}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦あり→ある：00006_aru⟧、⟦それぞれ→それぞれ：01453_sorezore⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{特別|とくべつ}→特別：01120_tokubetsu⟧な⟦{料理|りょうり}→料理：01523_ryouri⟧や⟦{飾|かざ}り→飾り：02539_kazari⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There are five seasonal festivals in Japan, each with its own special foods and decorations.

notes:
Originally from Chinese customs marking seasonal turning points. The five major {節句|せっく} ({五節句|ごせっく}) are:
- {人日|じんじつ} (January 7) — Seven Herb Festival
- {上巳|じょうし} (March 3) — {桃|もも}の{節句|せっく} (Girls' Day / Doll Festival)
- ⟦{端午|たんご}→端午：28695_tango⟧ (May 5) — {端午|たんご}の{節句|せっく} (Boys' Day / Children's Day)
- ⟦{七夕|たなばた}→七夕：05633_tanabata⟧ (July 7) — Star Festival
- {重陽|ちょうよう} (September 9) — Chrysanthemum Festival

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {桃|もも}の{節句|せっく}: Peach Festival (Girls' Day, March 3)
- {端午|たんご}の{節句|せっく}: Boys' Day (May 5)
- {五節句|ごせっく}: the five seasonal festivals
- {節句|せっく}⟦{料理|りょうり}→料理：01523_ryouri⟧: seasonal festival food
- {節句|せっく}⟦{飾|かざ}り→飾り：02539_kazari⟧: seasonal festival decorations

CULTURAL NOTE:
The March and May festivals remain widely celebrated in modern Japan. Families with daughters display ⟦{雛人形|ひなにんぎょう}→雛人形：14830_hinaningyou⟧ (hina dolls) in March, and families with sons display {鎧兜|よろいかぶと} (armor and helmets) or ⟦{鯉|こい}のぼり→鯉のぼり：05711_koinobori⟧ (carp streamers) in May.
